name: mc-rrr-content-authoring
description: Parse user-provided MC-RRR card text and author hero, scenario, encounter-set, and ability configurations using this project's existing effects.
---

# MC-RRR content authoring

Use this skill when a user provides card text or structured card data and asks to create or update a hero, scenario, encounter set, or its abilities and effects.

## Source of truth and interpretation

- Treat the user's supplied text, values, icons, traits, card counts, and images as authoritative. Do not infer missing information from artwork or outside sources.
- Consult `.junie/guidelines/translation-guide.md` for the input formats, official terminology, resource-icon notation, and code mapping.
- For ally shorthand such as `Attack: N[d]` or `Thwart: N[d]`, use `N` for the stat and set the corresponding consequential damage to 1; `[d]` does not mean N consequential damage. Only use another consequential-damage amount when it is explicitly supplied.
- If a supplied trait has no project constant or approved Spanish label, use a Spanish translation explicitly provided by the user; ask for one only when it is missing. Add or update the shared trait constant, label mapping, and translation tests. Update the translation guide unless the user explicitly prohibits changes to project rules.
- Preserve rules-bearing punctuation and connectors. A period keeps sentence order but does not create a success gate; independent effects joined by "and" resolve simultaneously; "Then" gates on full resolution and uses `thenEffect`; "instead" replaces rather than adds an effect. A comma alone has no timing meaning.
- If supplied text specifies a Response or Forced Response tied to another card's defeat, especially an attachment responding to its host's defeat, do not silently convert it to an Interrupt because of timing or cleanup concerns. Ask the user whether they intend a Forced Interrupt before changing the ability timing; keep the supplied response unless they confirm the conversion.
- Pay the printed resource cost of a played card and all resource costs in its `arrow` simultaneously. Represent "spend a [resource]" arrow costs with `EFFECT_SPEND` and the exact resource icon. Track payment by resource icon, not by whole card: a double-resource card can contribute one icon to each cost, and fixed costs consume only the icons assigned to their requirements. In simultaneous cost dialogs, let the player select individual icons; for variable `X` costs, the chosen icon count must not depend on which dialog they answer first. Keep unused icons available to later simultaneous costs, show only those remaining icons in the next payment dialog, and discard the physical card only once after all costs are committed. Compose arrow costs with `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS` when needed, and add a regression test when implementing a card with both costs.
- For a printed variable resource cost, configure `cost: RESOURCES_X`; X is the number of resource icons actually paid and is exposed as `playCardEffect.resourcesPaid`. If an effect's target count depends on that payment, defer target selection until after the cost and use `targetCountCalc` against `playCardEffect.resourcesPaid` with the appropriate multi-target selection. Preserve whether the printed text permits choosing fewer than X targets; use `selectUpTo` only when that is allowed.
- When printed text allows paying resources beyond a player card's cost, set `params.allowOverpay: true`. This enables payment selection even when the effective cost is 0 and consumes the selected resource icons; `playCardEffect.resourcesOverpaid` exposes the excess icons after the effective cost and resource requirements. Keep effective costs non-negative. For an interrupt to a card entering play, `TRIGGER_CARD_ENTER_PLAY` automatically matches the pre-entry window. Event cards have all their abilities initialized from hand, so do not set `workInHand` on an Event just to make its interrupt available from hand; for a non-Event source, set it only when its own interrupt must be registered before play.
- If an important value or rule interaction is missing or ambiguous, ask before choosing an interpretation. Do not invent card text, stats, traits, icons, keywords, or effects.
- For encounter cards with no supplied printed boost value, configure `boost: 0`; this does not omit a separately supplied Boost ability.
- Default booleans to `false`. Set them to `true` only when the text or rules explicitly require it. Do not infer that a later main-scheme stage is final.
- Store printed keyword flags under `params.keywords`, not as top-level card parameters.

## Authoring workflow

1. Identify whether each supplied card belongs to a hero, an aspect, a scenario, a modular encounter set, or a shared encounter-card definition. Inspect nearby catalog modules and tests before adding a new pattern.
2. Map the supplied facts into the existing card types, `params`, ability types, triggers, and effect types. Use domain constants imported from `mc-shared`; use `TARGET_*` constants for every field named `target`.
3. Prefer existing generic effects and compose them according to the card text. Do not create card-specific effect classes or branches in general abilities, effects, or factories. If required behavior is missing, implement a reusable effect and test it.
   Do not declare helper functions at module scope in ability, effect, or factory implementation files. Put reusable helpers in `utils/` and keep class-specific helpers as `static` methods.
4. Keep card definitions and counts in the appropriate catalog. Reuse a shared encounter-card definition from `catalog/encounters/` when needed, but omit `params.set` there; use `withCardSet(card, set)` in each consuming catalog to assign its set, and configure its count in each owning catalog.
5. Add or update catalog/runtime tests for the content. Compile every configured ability and verify its `effect` is one runnable effect instance with a callable `canRun`; exercise runtime-dependent paths through the real ability or effect.

For repository-wide workflow and architectural requirements, also follow `.github/skills/repo-working-guidelines/SKILL.md`.

## Aspect card definitions

- Put aspect card definitions in the shared type module under `packages/back/mc-data/seed/catalog/aspects/<aspect>/`, such as `allies.js`, `events.js`, `supports.js`, or `upgrades.js`. Do not create hero-named aspect modules or define aspect cards in hero catalogs.
- A hero's `config.precon` may reference shared aspect-card IDs, but the card definitions themselves must not be tied to that hero.
- `params.classification` accepts one classification as a string or multiple classifications as an array. Consumers must match each classification without assuming the field is always a string.
- Exception for hero-owned cards with an aspect classification: keep the card in that hero's `config.cards` with its printed hero set and count, and set `params.classification` to both `CLASSIFICATION_HERO` and the shared constant for its printed aspect (for example, `[CLASSIFICATION_HERO, CLASSIFICATION_AGGRESSION]`). This makes it a fixed card in that hero's deck while allowing hero- and aspect-specific abilities to recognize it; do not add a duplicate shared aspect definition.

### Team-Up (Equipo)

- Consult the Team-Up/Equipo rule in `docs/02-08-KEYWORDS-STATUS.md`; do not change the rules document when authoring a card.
- Preserve the two printed character names as `params.keywords.teamUp: ['Name 1', 'Name 2']`. Team-Up is not a trait and should not be reduced to a card-specific `paramsToPlay` condition.
- Enforce both rule checks generically: the selected hero's name, identity name, or related alter-ego name must match either Team-Up name for deck inclusion, and both names must match distinct friendly characters currently in play by printed title (`name`) or subtitle.
- Keep any printed `Maximum 1 per deck` separate as `params.maximum: {count: 1, target: TARGET_DECK}`. Preserve the normal aspect/basic catalog location and have only eligible heroes reference the card from their precon.
- Test deck-editor keyword preservation, eligible and ineligible hero deck limits, and playability with missing, enemy-only, and both friendly characters present.

## Hero definitions

- Add or update the hero under `packages/back/mc-data/seed/catalog/heroes/`, following a nearby hero module's structure.
- Keep the identity's two sides in `config.sides`, with the alter-ego and hero card types and their printed stats, traits, keywords, and abilities.
- Put the hero's fixed cards in `config.cards`, its deck references in `config.precon`, its obligation in `config.obligation`, and its full nemesis encounter set in `config.nemesis`.
- Use the hero's stable catalog ID and existing naming, image, and card-count conventions. Do not put hero-only setup into a scenario or a modular set.
- For nemesis-minion identification and the resolution of the remaining nemesis set, follow [Nemesis sets](#nemesis-sets).
- Test the hero's catalog normalization and card/ability construction; test runtime behavior for any newly implemented ability.

## Scenario definitions

- Add or update the scenario under `packages/back/mc-data/seed/catalog/scenarios/`, following an existing scenario module.
- Put the scenario's villains in `config.villains`, main-scheme sides in `config.mainSchemes`, and its own encounter cards in `config.cards`. Scenario-owned cards use the scenario's printed set name in their card `params.set`.
- Define each scenario encounter card in a named `const`; keep `config.cards` as `{count, card}` references to those constants, separating the definition from its number of copies.
- Keep each scenario's `config.cards` entries sorted in ascending order by the numeric image code in `card.params.image`; preserve this ordering when adding or rearranging scenario cards.
- **Never add the scenario's own ID as a set in `config.sets` or `config.defaultSets`.** The scenario's cards are already supplied by `config.cards`; `sets` and `defaultSets` reference separate registered encounter-set configurations, not the scenario itself.
- Keep `config.sets` and `config.defaultSets` limited to actual records in `packages/back/mc-data/seed/catalog/sets/`. Before finishing, verify every referenced set ID resolves to a registered set config. Do not add an empty or duplicate set just to satisfy an invalid scenario self-reference.
- Use `config.sets` / `config.defaultSets` for the separately configured encounter sets intended by the scenario, such as the Standard set and its modular set selection. Do not duplicate cards already in `config.cards`.
- Put scenario-owned cards that begin outside the game in `config.setAsideCards` as `{count, card}` entries. They are instantiated directly into `scenario.apart` and are not added to the encounter deck.
- Distinguish the player reference from the card criteria in a search. If text identifies a player by Alter Ego, match the stable Alter Ego side name (`superhero.sides.0.name`) rather than the hero-side `mainName`, even when multiple players share a hero-side name. Search only the affected player's specified zones. For a named-card search, filter by the printed name and only by additional card characteristics explicitly stated by the text; do not infer `isAlly` or `CLASSIFICATION_HERO` from the player reference. Apply the referential-ability hierarchy from the rules: the source card first, then cards associated with the same superhero/set, then cards of the same player/encounter category as the source. Only matches in the highest available tier qualify; keep all matches in that tier available for player choice unless the effect explicitly uses `firstMatch`.
- Represent each main-scheme stage as an A/B card pair in `config.mainSchemes`; put initial villain-stage selection and setup on the A side, and threat values and ongoing responses on the B side. Set `final: true` on a B side only when completing that stage explicitly ends the game; the scenario engine treats completion of that side as the end of the game.
- Preserve printed card counts, images, and set names. Do not infer that the scenario's next stage is final or that a modular set is mandatory unless the supplied rules say so.
- Map a printed Crisis icon on a side scheme (`[c]`) to `icons: {crisis: true}`.
- Test the scenario's normalized config and actual scenario-creation path. Verify its own cards are included once and only valid registered encounter sets are loaded.

### Split scenario play areas

- For scenarios that separate players into distinct play areas, use the generic `ScenarioZone` runtime and enable `separatePlayAreas`; do not change game-rule documents or introduce card-specific zone branches.
- Keep the encounter deck and phase sequence shared. Main schemes, Villains, encounter cards, Crisis/acceleration icons, searches, and non-global triggers resolve in the acting player's zone. Hazard icons are global because all zones draw from the shared encounter deck.
- Use `EFFECT_START_SCENARIO_SPLIT` to assign unused main-scheme stages to players in first-player order, and `EFFECT_ADVANCE_MAIN_SCHEME_STAGE` to reveal a later stage in a specified zone. Keep per-player stages in `allMainSchemes` and mark selected or unused stages so they cannot be reused.
- Use `EFFECT_MERGE_SCENARIO_ZONE` at the printed timing window. Each surviving player in a completed zone chooses a destination; player-linked cards follow their player, common cards follow the global first player's destination, and an all-defeated zone transfers nobody and is removed.
- A hub main scheme can prohibit joining through zone-destination filtering. Once all living players have joined the hub, advance its main scheme; do not make split-zone main-scheme threat values per-player unless the printed value includes the per-player symbol.
- In scenarios with separated play areas, abilities from cards in a player zone resolve only for that zone by default. Set `globalScope: true` only when the scenario rules make that ability apply across zones, as with Kang II's acceleration-token replacement. Cards in the unoccupied shared scenario hub can resolve across player zones, but player-target selectors still offer only players in the initiating player's zone. Constant validations such as `EFFECT_CANNOT_TARGET` must evaluate their condition in the source card's zone.
- When a scenario redirects acceleration tokens, use the generic `TRIGGER_WOULD_ADD_ACCELERATION_TOKEN` window and `EFFECT_REPLACE_EFFECT`; set `countFromEffect: true` on the replacement to preserve a calculated token count. Filter the trigger to other schemes when the text says “another scheme.”
- If setup removes player Obligations from the encounter deck, configure a setup ability on the initial main scheme that searches for and removes each player's Obligation; do not add an `excludeObligations` scenario property. For per-player Nemesis Minions, search the affected player's Nemesis collection when needed and then engage the exact selected minion; do not cache Nemesis Minions on the player.
- Test isolated scheme/villain lookup, local and global triggers, random stage assignment without reuse, individual destination choices, common-card routing, all-defeated cleanup, hub convergence, and the exact fixed/scaled threat values.

### Scenario auxiliary decks

- Put a required auxiliary-deck set in `config.sets`, not `config.defaultSets`; do not use `config.extraDecks` to reference it. Add an `ABILITY_SETUP` to the appropriate main-scheme side and use `EFFECT_CREATE_EXTRA_DECK` with that set's ID to move its cards from the encounter deck into a runtime auxiliary deck.
- Auxiliary scenario decks are shuffled during setup and displayed separately. By default, they do not expose their own discard pile; cards discarded from them go to the encounter deck's discard pile. Obtain a card with `EFFECT_GET_ENCOUNTER_CARD` using `from: PLACE_SCENARIO_EXTRA_DECK` and its configured `deckId`, then pass `effects.0.card` to `EFFECT_REVEAL_ENCOUNTER`. The reveal effect shows and resolves the supplied card without managing its source.
- When the scenario rules require an auxiliary deck to collect cards that enter play later, configure `collectCondition` and `hasDiscard: true` on `EFFECT_CREATE_EXTRA_DECK`; matching cards that leave play go to that deck's discard pile. Decks automatically shuffle their own discard to cycle when they run out of cards; do not configure a separate cycling flag. Test initial separation, cards entering play from elsewhere, discard routing, cycling, and presentation.
- When setup creates a deck from only some scenario-owned encounter cards, use `EFFECT_CREATE_EXTRA_DECK` with a non-empty `cardCondition` and a user-facing `name`. Scope the condition by printed set and card type (for example, `{set: SET, isSideScheme: true}`), and run it after any matching card that starts in play has been put into play. The filtered deck may be empty in an intentionally partial scenario; reveal its top card with the same `EFFECT_GET_ENCOUNTER_CARD` / `EFFECT_REVEAL_ENCOUNTER` flow.

### Hero-owned auxiliary decks

- Put a hero-owned auxiliary deck in the hero configuration's `extraDecks` array with an `id`, user-facing `name`, and normalized card entries. Do not put those cards in the normal player deck or in a scenario set.
- Player auxiliary decks have their own discard pile and are initialized with `topCardFaceUp: true`; serialize and render the top card separately from the facedown stack. Their discard pile must not be routed to the player's normal discard.
- Use `TARGET_PLAYER_EXTRA_DECK` or `TARGET_PLAYER_EXTRA_DECK_DISCARD` with the effect's `deckId` for generic deck operations. Add `position: TARGET_TOP_CARD` when the effect must target the auxiliary deck's top card; do not create a top-card-specific target or a Doctor-Strange-specific branch.
- Use `EFFECT_GET_TOP_CARD` with `target: TARGET_PLAYER_EXTRA_DECK` to take the deck's top card, and use `position: TARGET_TOP_CARD` only on effects such as `EFFECT_PAY_PRINTED_COST` or `EFFECT_RESOLVE_SPECIAL_ABILITY` that directly target that top card. Use `EFFECT_MOVE_TO_DECK` with the auxiliary-deck target to return a resolved card, and parameterize `EFFECT_RETURN_FACEDOWN` with a destination target when a facedown card stored under a host returns to a deck.
- Test deck initialization, top-card serialization, independent discard/cycling, refresh routing, and the exact card identity across remove/resolve/return operations.

### Tucked cards

- Tucked cards are faceup and stored in the host card's `tuckedCards` collection. Use `EFFECT_TUCK_UNDER` with the exact selected card objects; it can move cards directly from a player's hand, deck, discard pile, or another host's tucked collection.
- To let a host grant play permission to cards tucked beneath it, configure `playTuckedCardsCondition` on that host with the generic card condition (for example, `{isEvent: true, traits: TRAIT_ARROW}`). This permission is scoped to cards under that host; do not add a global play-from-tucked permission to matching card definitions.
- The play-from-tucked flow uses `PLACE_TUCKED`, surfaces playability in the tucked-card viewer, removes the card from the host while it is being played, restores its original position if play is cancelled, and discards a successfully played Event normally. Test matching and non-matching cards, another host, serialization/playability, and cancellation restoration.
- When a host leaves play, its tucked cards are discarded through the normal host cleanup. Do not move a searched deck card through the player's hand just to tuck it.

### Searching and looking at decks

- When a search examines any part of a deck, shuffle that entire deck after the full game step or card ability resolves, even if the printed text does not repeat the instruction. `EFFECT_SEARCH_CARDS` automatically shuffles searched decks after the enclosing resolution, following dependent card movement; do not add a second `EFFECT_SHUFFLE_DECK`. If another search mechanism does not shuffle automatically, put `EFFECT_SHUFFLE_DECK` after dependent movement in the `EFFECT_CHAINED`.
- Looking at cards in a deck is different: return those cards in the same order and do not shuffle unless the text explicitly instructs it.
- For “each player chooses up to N cards from their discard pile, adds them to their deck, and shuffles it,” use `EFFECT_FOR_EACH` with `target: TARGET_ALL_PLAYERS`. Inside it, chain `EFFECT_SEARCH_CARDS` for `PLACE_DISCARD_PILE` with `count: N` and `upTo: true`, then `EFFECT_MOVE_TO_DECK` with `target: TARGET_YOU`, `cards: 'selectedCards'`, and `position: DECK_POSITION_SHUFFLE`. The move effect performs the required shuffle even when the player chooses no cards; ensure the search result is an empty array in that case so the source card is not mistaken for the selected card.
- When each player discards cards from their own deck and places threat for distinct resource types in that player’s discarded batch, use `EFFECT_FOR_EACH` with `TARGET_ALL_PLAYERS`; inside each iteration, chain `EFFECT_DISCARD_FROM_DECK` and `EFFECT_PLACE_THREAT` with `paramsCalc: {target: 'effects.0.cards', formula: CALC_DIFFERENT_RESOURCE_TYPE}`. This keeps the resource count scoped to that player’s cards.

## Ability and effect composition

- Consult `.junie/guidelines/translation-guide.md`, `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md`, `.junie/guidelines/targets-guide.md`, and `docs/02-06-ABILITIES-EFFECTS.md` when mapping or changing card abilities.
- For a printed Hero Resource ability, use `ABILITY_HERO_RESOURCE` with its generated `resource`; put printed costs such as exhausting the source in `arrow` (for example, `EFFECT_EXHAUST` targeting `TARGET_THIS`). When the resource is restricted to Aspect cards, condition it on `cardToPay.card.classification` matching `ASPECT_IDS`, and test resource availability against Aspect and non-Aspect cards as well as hero/alter-ego form.
- For a printed generic Resource ability, use `ABILITY_RESOURCE`; configure its generated `resource`, printed costs in `arrow`, and any payment restriction in `condition` (for example, `{'cardToPay.isEvent': true, 'cardToPay.traits': TRAIT_THWART}`). Test resource availability with matching and non-matching payment cards and verify the configured arrow cost.
- Add `LABEL_ATTACK` or `LABEL_THWART` only when the supplied card text explicitly labels the ability as `(attack)` or `(thwart)` (including localized equivalents such as `(ataque)` or `(intervención)`). Never infer these labels from damage, threat removal, targets, or effect types; without an explicit label in the text, leave them off.
- For multiple consecutive player attacks, use one `EFFECT_DEAL_DAMAGE` with `isAttack: true` per attack in an `EFFECT_CHAINED`, preserving the printed order and separate attack windows. Do not use `EFFECT_SEVERAL_ATTACKS`, which resolves attacks by multiple enemies. Keep the enclosing ability unlabelled unless the card explicitly labels that ability as an attack.
- For healing up to a calculated number of friendly characters, use `EFFECT_HEAL` with a multi-character target, `multipleTarget: true`, `targetCountCalc`, and `selectUpTo: true`. `HealEffect` heals the configured amount from each chosen character and filters out characters that cannot be healed.
- For “exhaust a character you control for each [countable element]” without an explicit “choose,” calculate the count and make one multi-target selection with `EFFECT_EXHAUST`, `target: TARGET_ALL_CHARACTERS_YOU_CONTROL`, `multipleTarget: true`, and `targetCountCalc`; do not use `EFFECT_FOR_EACH` to select a character separately per iteration. For a single controlled character, use the same target with `selectCount: 1`. `EFFECT_EXHAUST` filters out characters already exhausted and exhausts all eligible characters if fewer than the calculated count remain.
- Use `EFFECT_CHAINED` for ordered or data-dependent effects and `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS` for independent effects joined by "and". Do not assign an array directly to `ability.effect`.
- For “discard a status card” effects, use `EFFECT_REMOVE_STATUS` and restrict its `statuses` to the types named in the text (for example, `[STATUS_STUNNED, STATUS_CONFUSED, STATUS_TOUGH]`, imported from `mc-shared`); target the character specified by the text. The effect selects and removes one matching status card.
- When a character gains a trait for a duration, use `EFFECT_LASTING` with the matching `TIME_*` duration and an `EFFECT_ADD_TRAIT` targeting that character; do not model a trait as a keyword.
- For an ongoing modifier or text-blanking effect that applies only while its source is in play, use an `ABILITY_CONSTANT` and a source-backed generic modifier. If applicability can change while the source stays in play, put the condition in `modifierCondition` so it is reevaluated dynamically, rather than relying only on entry-time target selection. Do not wrap it in `EFFECT_LASTING` merely to clean it up when the source leaves play; reserve `EFFECT_LASTING` for an explicit duration or expiry trigger. Test that the modifier stops applying as soon as its source leaves play.
- For a Response after you use one of your hero's basic attributes, use `ABILITY_HERO_RESPONSE` with the applicable `TRIGGER_YOU_BASIC_*` values. If one shared limit covers several attributes, put those triggers on one ability and use `limit: {count: 1, target: TARGET_PHASE}`.
- For a Response after a character actually becomes ready, use `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_READIED`; `EFFECT_READY` exposes the cards it truly readied in `effect.readiedTargets`. Filter that path when the response is limited to a named character, and test that an already-ready or canceled target does not trigger it.
- When a boost-icon count from a discarded encounter-card batch modifies the stat currently being used, use the matching stat trigger and chain `EFFECT_DISCARD_FROM_DECK` before the corresponding `EFFECT_MODIFY_*_VALUE`. Calculate the bonus with `CALC_BOOST_ICONS` from `effects.0.cards`, and test the actual chained effect context.
- When a card repeats a selection process (as specified for Mercurio's «Por partida doble»), wrap one `EFFECT_CHOOSE_ABILITY` in `EFFECT_REPEAT` with the required count so the player chooses again during each repetition. Do not wrap each option in a repeat effect.
- For "remove a total of N threat among all schemes," use `EFFECT_ASSIGN_THREAT` with `target: TARGET_ALL_SCHEMES`; it presents a shared assignment dialog for eligible schemes and resolves each allocation through `EFFECT_REMOVE_THREAT`. If the event is dragged onto an eligible scheme, prioritize that scheme for the dialog's initial allocation without limiting the effect to that scheme.
- For "remove N threat per player" with `EFFECT_REMOVE_THREAT`, use `threat: [N, true]`; `RemoveThreatEffect` scales it by `match.numPlayers`. Test the actual effect with multiple players.
- To reduce the hand size of the player engaged with an encounter minion, configure an `ABILITY_CONSTANT` on that minion with `TRIGGER_GET_HAND_SIZE`, `triggerParams: {target: TARGET_ENGAGED}`, and `EFFECT_MODIFY_HAND_SIZE` targeting `TARGET_EFFECT` with a negative `count`. Test the actual hand-size calculation for the engaged player, another player, and after the minion is no longer engaged.
- For a Boost ability that gives the Villain a Tough status and another boost card for the current activation, use `ABILITY_BOOST` with an `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS` containing `EFFECT_TOUGH` and `EFFECT_DEAL_BOOST`, both targeted at `TARGET_VILLAIN`. `EFFECT_DEAL_BOOST` appends to the activation being resolved; use `EFFECT_STORE_BOOST` only when the card text gives a boost for a later activation.
- Distinguish revealing an encounter minion from putting it into play. Use `EFFECT_SEARCH_CARD_REVEAL` when the text searches for and reveals a card; the normal reveal process resolves its "When Revealed" abilities. `EFFECT_SEARCH_CARD_REVEAL` collapses duplicate copies by printed name and automatically selects when only one distinct name matches; it keeps a dialog when different names remain, so do not configure `firstMatch` for this effect. After `EFFECT_DISCARD_UNTIL` selects a minion that remains in the encounter discard pile, first take that exact card with `EFFECT_GET_ENCOUNTER_CARD` from `PLACE_ENCOUNTER_DISCARD` and `cardSource: 'selectedCard'`, then pass `effects.0.card` to `EFFECT_REVEAL_ENCOUNTER`; this removes the card from its source before revealing it. Set `player` to a runtime path such as `match.initialPlayer` when the text specifies who resolves the reveal; do not wrap a single player in `EFFECT_FOR_EACH` solely to establish that context. For a minion explicitly put into play engaged, use `EFFECT_ENGAGE` without a reveal effect; "When Revealed" abilities do not trigger. `EngageEffect` shows the post-entry dialog even for minions from `scenario.apart`, unless that minion was already shown in a reveal dialog. If the rules instruct a player to find and reveal a minion already in play, engage it and resolve its reveal-triggered abilities without treating it as entering play.
- Resolve pronouns such as “ese enemigo”, “ese Plan”, or “esa carta” against the exact target already selected. Give the enclosing chain and dependent effects the same target selector so the engine reuses the selection; do not open a second unrelated target dialog.
- Treat “adicional” as a modifier of the effect immediately named before it. Include the base and additional amount in one effect; for a fixed base with a calculated increase, use `damage` with `additionalDamageCalc` on `EFFECT_DEAL_DAMAGE` or `threat` with `additionalThreatCalc` on `EFFECT_REMOVE_THREAT`, so `max` applies only to the increase. Use `paramsCalc` when it calculates the full amount. Do not create a second target selection or a separate unrelated effect.
- When `EFFECT_MOVE_TO_DECK` receives a card list and uses `DECK_POSITION_SHUFFLE`, it already adds the cards and shuffles the deck. Do not append a separate `EFFECT_SHUFFLE_DECK` for that same operation; use `EFFECT_CHAINED` only when other ordered steps still need to precede or follow the move.
- During an enemy attack, stop the activation as soon as its attacker leaves play: do not resolve later attack steps or the attack-end triggers, and leave the attack unresolved. A defeated minion always stops its activation. If a defeated Villain advances to a same-title stage, treat that stage as the same attacker and continue with it; a different-title stage or a completed game stops the activation. Recheck after interrupt/response windows and each awaited attack step, and test minion defeat, same-title continuation, different-title transition, and final Villain defeat.
- For "look at the top N cards, discard one, and return the rest in any order," use the reusable `EFFECT_SELECT_AND_ORDER_TOP_CARDS` and explicitly select the deck with `target` (for example, `TARGET_ENCOUNTER_DECK`); do not discard the entire group or silently preserve its original order.
- For damage that ignores a Tough status without discarding it, configure `ignoreTough: true` on `EFFECT_DEAL_DAMAGE`; do not use Piercing, which consumes the Tough status.
- When an enemy attack gains Piercing from an attachment or modifier, test a full attack against a Tough character: Tough is discarded and positive damage is dealt, but Tough remains if all damage is prevented.
- Use `CALC_DIFFERENT_CARD_TYPES` to count distinct printed types in a card list, and `match.inPlayCards` to count traits across all cards in play instead of rebuilding zone lists. A main-scheme attachment that raises its completion threshold uses `attach: TARGET_MAIN_SCHEME` and `threatThresholdModifier`.
- Put a "Then" clause in `thenEffect`; do not use it for ordinary ordered sentences. Model "if no effect occurred" fallbacks by attempting the effect and then checking its runtime result, not by prechecking whether a target exists.
- Use the correct ability timing and trigger for the printed text. Do not replace a forced ability with an optional one, or implement ongoing prohibitions as forced interrupts.
- For "when the attached character would ready, discard this card instead," use `ABILITY_FORCED_INTERRUPT` with `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_WOULD_READY`, `triggerParams.target: TARGET_ATTACHED`, and `EFFECT_REPLACE_EFFECT` targeting `TARGET_EFFECT` with an `EFFECT_DISCARD_GAME` replacement targeting `TARGET_THIS`. This window belongs to `EFFECT_READY`, not to a phase: it applies to preparation from card abilities as well as game steps. Test a real card ability during a turn (including its costs), both identities, end-of-phase preparation, multiple copies, and replacement of only the host in a multi-character ready. A Boost attachment enters play through `EFFECT_PUT_PLAY` with `cardSource: 'card'`, the printed host target, and `controller: 'match.scenario'`; test through a real enemy activation so boost cleanup preserves it.
- For a response after a numbered Villain-phase step, use `TRIGGER_VILLAIN_PHASE_STEP` with `condition: {step: n}`; it fires after that step resolves and before the next begins.
- For a response after a character is defeated or schemes, use `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_DEFEATED` or `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_SCHEMES` and set `triggerParams.characterType` when the text names a specific character type. Set `controlledByYou: true` for a defeat response that requires a character you control. Use `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_TAKES_DAMAGE` for a response only after positive damage is actually suffered; its context includes the affected character, damage amount, and attack context when applicable.
- For an attachment that modifies its host's attack, stuns a Hero damaged by that attack, and discards after it, preserve the printed Forced Interrupt for the attack modifier and register `EFFECT_DELAYED` on `TARGET_EFFECT` for the later discard of `TARGET_CARD`. Gate that cleanup with `EFFECT_DO_IF` and `{'effect.canceled': false}` so a canceled activation does not consume the attachment. Resolve the damage-dependent clause through a hidden `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_TAKES_DAMAGE` Forced Response with `triggerParams: {target: TARGET_ALL_HEROES, attacker: TARGET_ATTACHED}` and `condition: {'effect.isAttack': true}`. Use `TARGET_TRIGGERED_TARGET` for that exact damaged Hero; cover both direct damage and Overkill arrays, prevention, other attackers, and source cleanup.
- For a response after a side scheme is defeated, use `TRIGGER_SIDE_SCHEME_DEFEATED`; it fires after an actual side-scheme defeat, including the automatic defeat when its threat reaches zero. Do not use `TRIGGER_THIS_DEFEAT`, which is scoped to the source card itself.
- For a Response after a specific character uses a basic power, configure separate abilities on that character for `TRIGGER_THIS_ATTACK` and `TRIGGER_THIS_THWARTS`, each with `condition: {'effect.ability.isBasic': true}`. These source-specific triggers restrict the response to the character that owns it; do not use `TRIGGER_YOU_BASIC_ATTACK` or `TRIGGER_YOU_BASIC_THWART` for an ally's own basic power. Test basic and non-basic uses and a different character's use.
- A stunned hero or ally may attempt an attack without a legal enemy target, and a confused hero or ally may attempt a thwart without a legal scheme target. In either case, pay the attempt's costs (including exhaustion) and remove the matching status instead of resolving the attack/thwart; do not fabricate a target or resolve attack/thwart consequences.
- Do not set `workInHand: true` on an Event merely because its ability must work from hand: `Hand.addCard` initializes all Event abilities from hand automatically. For an ability on another player-card type that must apply while its source is in hand or while the card is played from another supported location (for example, a printed reduction to its own play cost), set `workInHand: true`. `PlayCardEffect` ensures marked abilities are registered before calculating the cost; temporary triggers are removed if the play fails and the card returns outside the hand, while the trigger persists if the card enters play. `TRIGGER_CARD_ENTER_PLAY` selects the pre-entry window for Interrupt and Forced Interrupt abilities and the post-entry window for Response and Forced Response abilities.
- For an ability that modifies the cost of playing its own non-Event card, combine `workInHand: true` with `TRIGGER_THIS_PLAY_CARD`; this scopes the modifier to the exact card being played. Event abilities are already registered from hand for hand-origin plays. For an effect that says "after you play a card," use the player-scoped end-of-play trigger so it resolves after the card finishes playing without responding to another player's card.
- For an interrupt that lets a character use ATK instead of INT while thwarting a specific scheme, use `TRIGGER_SCHEME_GET_THWART` on that scheme and `EFFECT_SET_THWART_VALUE` against `TARGET_EFFECT`. Calculate the replacement with `CALC_ATTACK` from `triggeredEffect.selectedTarget`; the non-forced `ABILITY_INTERRUPT` is the optional choice, so do not wrap it in `EFFECT_MAY`. Test that the effect applies only while thwarting its source scheme.
- For a constant ability that says the character may use ATK instead of INT during a basic thwart, wrap `EFFECT_SET_THWART_VALUE` in `EFFECT_MAY`, use `TRIGGER_SCHEME_GET_THWART`, and keep the constant trigger hidden so its May opens the single confirmation after effective INT is calculated. Calculate ATK with `CALC_ATTACK`; show the plan and both values, and keep the action as a thwart so attack-action interrupts do not resolve while thwart triggers still do.
- For "after you play [a named card] from your hand," use `TRIGGER_YOU_END_PLAY_CARD` and filter the played card through the play effect, for example `condition: {'effect.card.name': cardName}`. `PlayCardEffect` clears `removedFromHand` before this end trigger resolves, so do not use that field as the condition. Cards with no `playFrom` entries are only playable from hand; if another origin is supported, do not claim a hand-only restriction without a runtime origin signal.
- For "exhaust one Ally you control," use the singular `TARGET_ALLY_YOU_CONTROL`; `TARGET_ALL_ALLIES_YOU_CONTROL` exhausts a group and is not interchangeable.
- Keep all effect configuration generic and target-driven. Preserve the selected target identified by the text; do not ask for an unrelated second selection.
- For a target defined by a negative card condition (for example, a Minion that is not Elite), use `not` in a generic condition with `TARGET_CONDITION_CARD`, and constrain it to the relevant in-play card type. Do not add a card-specific target selector or discard effect.
- When a persistent card's own attacks gain keywords, register an `ABILITY_CONSTANT` on `TRIGGER_THIS_ATTACK` and use `EFFECT_MODIFY_ATTACK` against `TARGET_EFFECT` with `modify: {keywords: {...}}`; this trigger scopes the modifier to attacks made by that source card. If the text specifies only its basic attack, add `condition: {'effect.ability.isBasic': true}`. Do not put attack-only keywords in the character's `params.keywords`, which assigns them to the character rather than its attack effect. For a player Event's own attack, configure the keyword in that attack's `EFFECT_DEAL_DAMAGE` `params.keywords` instead: the Event leaves the hand and its triggers end before its effect resolves.
- When an attack gains a keyword based on the trait of the player card that originates it (for example, an Event or Upgrade), use `TRIGGER_YOU_ATTACK` with an `ABILITY_CONSTANT`, condition on `effect.ability.card.traits`, and modify `TARGET_EFFECT` with `EFFECT_MODIFY_ATTACK`. The same trigger may be emitted in the initial and end windows: constants/interrupts resolve at initiation, while `ABILITY_RESPONSE` resolves at the end; do not create separate trigger names for those priorities or infer the source-card trait from the attacking hero or ally.
- When an attachment continuously grants keywords to each Villain attack, register an `ABILITY_CONSTANT` on `TRIGGER_VILLAIN_ATTACKS` and use `EFFECT_MODIFY_ATTACK` against `TARGET_EFFECT`, putting every granted keyword (for example, `ranged` and `piercing`) in `modify.keywords`; do not model the keyword gain itself as a forced interrupt. The engine applies newly attached modifiers to an attack already in progress and evaluates source-backed keywords when they are used, so do not add a card-specific Boost effect to modify the current activation. Keyword modifiers merge so separate attachments preserve each other's keywords and stop applying when their source leaves play.
- For scenario attachments linked to a Villain, use `attach: TARGET_VILLAIN`; put printed ATK bonuses in the attachment's `params.attack` and numeric keywords granted to the attached character (such as Retaliate) in `params.keywords`. Map explicitly printed traits such as Habilidad to their `TRAIT_*` constants. Set `boost` to the supplied printed value and configure `boostAbility` only when a Boost ability is supplied; do not infer uniqueness. Use the Villain-attack constant pattern above for keywords that belong to its attacks, not to the Villain itself.
- For a forced Villain-activation interrupt that adds a runtime number of boost cards, use `TRIGGER_VILLAIN_ACTIVATES` and `EFFECT_DEAL_BOOST` with `paramsCalc` (for example, `CALC_COUNT` on `match.sideSchemes`). Put any printed "Then" cleanup in `thenEffect`; a calculated count of zero still resolves and allows that cleanup. For "maximum once per activation," use `maximum: {count: 1, target: TARGET_ACTIVATION}`; enemy activation effects clear that scope when the activation ends.
- If a calculation counts cards in `card.attached` but the text names only Attachments, filter with `conditions: {isAttachment: true}` so other attached cards do not count; test with both kinds in the runtime collection.
- For a Hero Action on an encounter attachment, configure fixed resource-icon costs with `EFFECT_SPEND` and the exact icons. If it also requires exhausting the hero, compose `EFFECT_EXHAUST` and `EFFECT_SPEND` in an `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS` arrow cost. Keep any post-payment discard in the ability's effect so all costs are paid before the source leaves play.
- For a forced interrupt that reflects damage from an attached Villain, use `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_WOULD_TAKE_DAMAGE` with `triggerParams.target: TARGET_ATTACHED` and filter attack damage with `condition: {'effect.isAttack': true}`. Read the pending amount from `triggeredTargetDamage` and use `EFFECT_REPLACE_EFFECT` to replace the original damage with `EFFECT_TAKE_DAMAGE` against `TARGET_YOUR_SUPERHERO`; the replacement's `thenEffect` handles printed cleanup such as discarding the attachment. Test attack and non-attack damage through the actual trigger context and verify the source leaves play.
- For "when [character] is attacked," use `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_ATTACKED` with `triggerParams.target` selecting that character (`TARGET_ATTACHED` for an attachment's host). This window does not require positive damage; a stunned attempt is not an attack. For a maximum shared by all same-title copies per triggering attack, use `maximum: {count: 1, target: TARGET_EFFECT}`. Put a printed self-discard arrow in `arrow`, and compose independent prevention and reflected damage with `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS`, `EFFECT_PREVENT_DAMAGE` (`preventAll: true` for all damage), and non-attack `EFFECT_DEAL_DAMAGE` against `TARGET_ATTACKER`. Test zero damage, multiple copies, a subsequent attack, the exact hero/ally attacker, and source cleanup. Ordinary simultaneous effects preserve the incoming trigger's effect context; cost-payment sessions use their own effect only when resolving costs.
- In `EFFECT_PREVENT_DAMAGE` and `EFFECT_PREVENT_PLACE_DAMAGE`, reserve `preventAll: true` for explicit total prevention. Its default is `false`; `damage: 0`, an omitted amount, or a `paramsCalc` result of 0 never means all damage. Test zero and positive calculations through the actual effect context and preserve the same calculation in any confirmation preview.
- When behavior depends on runtime paths such as `paramsCalc`, `targetCountCalc`, `condition`, `effectCondition`, `condition.exclude`, or `sourceIn`, add a regression test with the actual runtime context shape.
- Numeric keyword values support `[value, true]` for per-player scaling. Apply this consistently to numeric keywords, and verify `Uses` initializes the resulting counters and discards its card when the last counter is removed.
- Test changes to persistent scenario modifiers while their source is in play and after it leaves play.

### Obligation cards

- An obligation given to a player is put into that player's game zone and its abilities remain active there after its instant resolution. Do not discard it automatically just because its `TRIGGER_INSTANT` ability finished.
- An option that creates a persistent obligation effect must target the obligation card as its source, keep the card in play while the effect is active, and discard/remove the obligation only through an effect printed on that obligation (for example, an end-of-play response owned by the obligation).
- When a persistent option modifies the next card a player plays, scope the constant to the player's play trigger and the printed card condition, and ensure its cleanup targets the obligation rather than the player or the played card.

### Defeat trigger selection

Choose a defeat trigger by identifying who/what the ability text says defeats the target. Do not confuse a card's own defeat with that card defeating a minion:

| Trigger | Meaning and use |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIGGER_THIS_DEFEAT` | The card that owns the ability is itself being defeated. This is not minion-only; use it for `ABILITY_WHEN_DEFEATED` and other abilities on the defeated card (for example, a side scheme or a minion). `DefeatEffect` dispatches it in the forced-response and forced-interrupt windows before the card leaves play. |
| `TRIGGER_ATTACHED_DEFEAT` | The host of the source attachment is about to be defeated. Use it with `ABILITY_FORCED_INTERRUPT` for effects that resolve while the attachment is still linked; the interrupt runs before the host leaves play. Test through the actual host defeat. |
| `TRIGGER_ATTACHED_ACTIVATES` | The attached enemy has completed an activation. Use it with a Forced Response that should resolve after that specific enemy attacks or schemes; the trigger is scoped to the attachment's host and only fires when the activation resolved without cancellation or interruption. A stunned/confused skipped activation does not qualify. Test a matching host activation, another enemy's activation, and skipped/canceled activations. |
| `TRIGGER_CHARACTER_DEFEATED` | A character has actually been defeated. Use `triggerParams.characterType` to filter by printed card type and `controlledByYou: true` when the text requires control. This does not mean that the ability's source card is being defeated. |
| `TRIGGER_THIS_DEFEAT_MINION` | The ability's source card matches `params.card` in the defeat-effect context, and `effect.selectedTarget` must be a minion. Use it when the text says that this character/card defeats a minion (for example, Tigra); do not use it for that source card's own "When Defeated" ability. |
| `TRIGGER_YOU_DEFEAT_MINION` | `effect.character` must match the player or their superhero, and the defeated target must be a minion. Use it for player/superhero-specific text such as "after you defeat a minion," rather than text tied to a particular ally or card. |
| `TRIGGER_YOUR_HERO_ATTACK_DEFEAT_ENEMY` | The defeated target is an enemy and the defeating event is an attack initiated by your hero. Use only when the text specifically depends on your hero's attack defeating an enemy. |

Filter cards affected by the ability in its effect, not in the trigger. For example, a side scheme's "When Defeated" trigger remains `TRIGGER_THIS_DEFEAT`; its effect can separately filter discarded cards to Goblin minions.

## Cannot restrictions

- Treat "Cannot"/"No puede" as absolute; never make it optional with `EFFECT_MAY`.
- For ongoing restrictions, use `ABILITY_CONSTANT`. Do not use `ABILITY_FORCED_INTERRUPT` merely because the implementation checks an event before it resolves.
- If the restriction makes a card an illegal target, use `EFFECT_CANNOT_TARGET` in the constant ability's `validation`. Configure `effectTypes` or `effectCategories`; use `condition`, `targetCondition`, and `effectCondition` only for their documented scopes.
- For “cannot leave play while [a card] is in play,” use a constant `EFFECT_CANNOT_TARGET` validation on the protected card with `effectCategories: [EFFECT_CATEGORY_LEAVE_PLAY]`, and test the runtime condition against `match.inPlayCards`. Add new generic exit effects to that shared category instead of maintaining per-card effect-type lists. Include direct defeat paths such as a side scheme reaching zero threat; that automatic defeat must not inherit the thwart activation's target filter or repeat its activation windows, but must still preserve context for defeat triggers and honor the card's `EFFECT_CANNOT_TARGET` validations. For `EFFECT_MOVE_TO_DECK`, validate every card in its configured `cards` list as well as the destination target.
- For permission prohibitions, use `EFFECT_CANNOT` with the `restriction` key matching the permission context. Have the action check trigger constant abilities with that restriction initially allowed; do not add a separate collector just to carry the permission boolean.
- In scenarios with split play areas, the trigger system scopes card abilities to their source zone unless the ability sets `globalScope: true`; cards in the unoccupied shared scenario hub are available to all zones. Player-target selectors remain limited to the initiating player's zone regardless of that flag. Use `sourceIn` only when the restriction independently requires the source card to appear in a runtime collection. Prefer the generic `Trigger` over a subclass that only checks source membership or a named restriction, and test the actual ability in the relevant zone context.
- Ensure constant validations run for normal, preselected, and multi-target candidates before targets are shown or resolved.
- Test that a protected card is excluded when the condition is active, becomes a valid target when inactive, and does not exclude unrelated cards. If `condition`, `targetCondition`, or `effectCondition` reads runtime paths, test matching and non-matching values through the actual validation/target-resolution context.

## Effect target exclusions

- Prefer declarative `condition.exclude` paths over callbacks, card-specific fields, or effect-specific target filters.
- Configure `condition.exclude` with one runtime-context path or an array of paths. Use `*` to expand arrays, including results from earlier effects in an `EFFECT_CHAINED`.
- Example: to exclude players targeted by earlier attacks:

  ```js
  condition: {
      exclude: [
          'effects.0.attacks.*.selectedTarget',
          'effects.0.attacks.*.defender.owner',
      ],
  }
  ```

- Point paths to target objects, not only IDs; exclusion matches object identity or matching `id`.
- In every field named `target`, including `limit.target` and `maximum.target`, use a `TARGET_*` constant. Define limit/maximum scopes with `target`, never `time`. Add a `TARGET_*` alias in `mc-shared/constants/targets.js` if the needed scope has no constant. Effect `params.target` needs a resolver; limit/maximum scope targets are metadata and do not.
- A `limit` applies to its ability instance; a `maximum` aggregates matching card names. Do not branch on a particular selector in `ForEachEffect`; preserve normal target resolution order and filter its results.
- Validate that exclusion paths are non-empty strings. Test wildcard expansion, missing values, multiple paths, target matching, and the actual nesting of prior-effect results passed at runtime; a `path()` test or configuration assertion alone is insufficient. If route syntax or matching changes, update `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md` and its tests.

## Nemesis sets

- Keep the hero's complete nemesis encounter set in `config.nemesis`.
- If there is one minion, mark it with `params.nemesis: true`. If there are multiple minions, mark every minion whose printed parenthetical text identifies it as that hero's nemesis minion. Do not designate other minions based only on their inclusion in the set.
- When resolving Shadow of the Past, reveal every set-aside card matching `isMinion: true` and `isNemesis: true`, and reveal all nemesis side schemes.
- Move the remaining cards from the set-aside nemesis collection into the encounter deck and shuffle it. Use `EFFECT_INCLUDE_ASIDE_CARDS` followed by `EFFECT_SHUFFLE_DECK`, targeting `TARGET_SCENARIO`.
- Tie surge to whether a nemesis minion entered play, not to whether any set-aside card moved into the encounter deck.
- Test that every hero has a designated nemesis minion, that all printed nemesis minions are designated (including multiple-minion sets), and that Shadow of the Past reveals and shuffles the correct cards.

## Stored villain boosts

- For text that gives the Villain a facedown boost card for a later activation, use `EFFECT_STORE_BOOST` with the Villain as its target. Do not use `EFFECT_DEAL_BOOST`, which affects the activation currently resolving.
- Keep stored cards marked as future boosts so unrelated facedown cards on an enemy are not consumed accidentally.
- At the next Villain activation, move stored cards into that activation's boost list before its normal card. Resolve all boost cards in dealt order through the regular boost flow so printed values and boost abilities accumulate normally.
- Keep iteration live so boost abilities that append cards to the same activation resolve those cards too. Consume stored cards only when the activation resolves; a skipped activation leaves them stored.
- After resolution, use the regular boost-card discard/put-into-play handling.
- Serialize pending cards without face name or image, pass their encounter-card type through the Villain presentation, and render the encounter-card back. Display one back without a count and group multiple pending backs with a count.
- Test storage and order, resolution before the normal boost card, consumption, skipped activations, boost abilities that add cards, and identity-safe UI serialization.
